name: Player Leaderboard
author: tharkun69

sections.description:
Player Leaderboard provides a complete, free workflow for managing sports rankings in WordPress. Administrators create competitions, add players or teams, enter results and publish the calculated tables on any page or post.

The plugin supports singles, doubles and team competitions. Standings use configurable points for victories, defeats and draws. Individual and doubles rankings can take opponent strength, bonuses and rating history into account.

There is one free edition of Player Leaderboard. No premium edition or paid feature gate is required.

Features

  • Create singles, doubles and team competitions.
  • Manage players or teams and their contact information.
  • Record one result or up to ten results at once.
  • Configure points, sets, ratings, bonuses and ranking behaviour.
  • Display standings, rankings and duel matrices on the front end.
  • Optionally show result-detail dialogs.
  • Import and export competitions, players and results as CSV.
  • Configure table and matrix colours per competition.
  • Use responsive, horizontally scrollable tables without clipped columns.
  • Read expanded context-sensitive help and workflow guides while editing a competition.
  • View complete shortcode documentation in the competition overview and directly below the editor help.

Basic workflow

  1. Open Player Leaderboard in the WordPress administration area.
  2. Create a competition and select its type and scoring rules.
  3. Add the participating players or teams.
  4. Enter the match results.
  5. Copy the shortcode shown in the competition list to a page or post.

Shortcode

The competition ID is required:

[player_leaderboard id="1"]

Available attributes:

  • id – Numeric competition ID. Required.
  • mode – Output type: standing (default), ranking or matrix.
  • showheader – Set to true to show the competition title and view heading. Default: false.
  • details – Set to true to make standing or matrix values open result-detail dialogs. Default: false.
  • view – Ranking calculation shown for doubles: points (default), quotient, rating, ratings or average.
  • type – Matrix value: games (default), sets, points or rating.
  • matrix_font_size – Matrix font size in pixels from 8 to 32. If omitted, the responsive default size is used.
  • fontweight – Legacy responsive matrix font-size factor from 1 to 500. Default: 100.
  • width – Minimum matrix width with a supported CSS unit, for example 100%, 720px or 50rem. If less space is available, the matrix becomes horizontally scrollable. Default: 100%.

Examples:

[player_leaderboard id="1" mode="standing" showheader="true" details="true"]

[player_leaderboard id="1" mode="ranking" view="average"]

[player_leaderboard id="1" mode="matrix" type="sets" details="true" matrix_font_size="12" width="100%"]

CSV import and export

Use the CSV export generated by Player Leaderboard as the template for imports. A complete competition export can contain competition, player and result rows. During import you can choose whether existing rating values are reset and whether result rows are imported.

For security, CSV uploads are limited to .csv files up to 5 MB and are available only to administrators.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  2. Select the plugin ZIP file and choose Install Now.
  3. Activate Player Leaderboard.
  4. Open Player Leaderboard in the administration menu and create the first competition.

When the plugin is updated, its database schema is upgraded automatically. Deactivation keeps all data. Deleting the plugin through the WordPress plugin screen removes its competition, player and result tables.
sections.faq:
Is a paid or premium version required?

No. Player Leaderboard has one free edition and all included features are available in it.

Where do I find the competition ID?

The competition overview displays a ready-to-copy shortcode for every competition. The number in its id attribute is the competition ID.

Why does the shortcode display “Competition not found”?

Check that the numeric id in the shortcode belongs to an existing competition and that the competition was not deleted.

Can I keep my data while temporarily disabling the plugin?

Yes. Deactivation keeps the data. WordPress uninstall, which occurs when the plugin is deleted, removes the plugin tables permanently. Export a CSV first if you need a backup.

What should I use as a CSV import template?

Export a competition from Player Leaderboard and edit that file without changing its row tags or column order.
sections.changelog:
1.1

  • Updated plugin metadata and compatibility information for WordPress 7.0.2 and PHP 7.4 or newer.
  • Added complete installation, usage, shortcode, CSV and FAQ documentation.
  • Removed outdated premium-version references; the plugin has one free edition.
  • Added capability and nonce checks to all write operations, imports, recalculation and bulk deletion.
  • Hardened database queries, sorting, uploads, dynamic styles and output escaping.
  • Fixed a PHP 8 fatal error in front-end asset hooks.
  • Fixed the matrix rating calculation and possible division-by-zero errors.
  • Fixed the points-only path when entering multiple results.
  • Fixed player and competition deletion so dependent data is removed consistently.
  • Improved database indexes, redirects, date handling and PHP 8.4 CSV compatibility.
  • Added responsive overflow containers so wide frontend and administration tables remain fully accessible.
  • Added expanded context-sensitive help and workflow guides to the competition editor.
  • Added complete shortcode documentation to the competition overview and directly below the editor help.
  • Redesigned the encounter matrix with semantic table markup, compact 90-degree column labels, reliable horizontal scrolling, a clearer colour scale and improved keyboard accessibility.
  • Added the matrix_font_size shortcode parameter for an explicit matrix font size.
  • Fixed the competition editor page title so it shows the competition name while editing.

1.0.3

  • Fixed CVE-2025-12824.
  • Tested with WordPress 6.9.

1.0.2

  • Corrected button style usage.

1.0.1

  • Redesigned the administration screens.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with competition, player, result, standing, ranking and matrix features.
  • Corrected the plugin title and icon.
